claims.text: A novel hybrid-rolling process can introduce a dual-phase lamellar colony structure with numerous internal boundaries in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Introducing this dual-phase lamellar colony structure can increase strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Introducing this dual-phase lamellar colony structure can increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Numerous internal boundaries enhance the strength-ductility synergy of eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed strength and ductility improvements occur at room temperature.
The initial alloy already has a dual-phase lamellar colony structure.
The exact mechanism responsible for the proposed strength and ductility improvements is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy is stated to already possess the same dual-phase lamellar colony structure that the intervention is supposed to introduce, so the intervention does not define a distinct structural change.
The stated baseline is an unmodified lamellar-colony alloy, whereas the proposed control is an alloy without the dual-phase lamellar structure; these are not clearly the same control condition.
